hypothesis: Observed-only capital-allocation alpha: on the fixed cash-feasible champion cohort, for each same-day entry-slot conflict where an accepted default-off sleeve (sbc burden, supplier financing debt relief, distribution-day absorption, MOVE relief) generated a candidate on the exact date the core stack executed an entry, the sleeve candidate's settled matched-horizon net return should exceed the same-window return of the displaced core entry ticker, establishing entry-time cross-source slot arbitration as a viable new allocator mechanism.
alpha_hypothesis: If sleeve candidates carry more marginal information than the core entry they would displace, settled matched-horizon replacement value on actual same-day entry-slot conflicts should be positive in mean and median.

calibration.surprise_note: Two mild surprises: the aggregate mean was positive rather than negative, and sleeves clearly beat the SPY control on conflict days. The kill came exactly where predicted: the median pair and the late_strong window.

gate1.note: Observed-only attribution; champion baseline used as the core side of every pair, not re-measured.

gate2.note: No strategy fields touched; reads committed replay artifacts and warehouse OHLCV only.

gate3.note: No filter added; candidate pool unchanged; observed-only.

gate4.acceptance_rule: Lead only if mean AND median matched-horizon replacement value (sleeve minus core, both after 35bp) are positive, at least 2 of 3 windows have positive mean, and max single-pair share of aggregate positive replacement value <=50%. Otherwise rejected and the arbitration lane parks with a quantitative forward-conflict reopen count. Positive result stays a lead; no production or order change.

production_impact: none; trade_enabled unchanged; no orders, ranking, sizing, or exits altered
rejection_reason: Acceptance rule required mean AND median replacement value positive plus >=2 positive windows; median was -0.87% and late_strong mean was -8.07%, so entry-time displacement of core entries is rejected and the lane parks.

post_run_reflection.why_result_happened: On the majority of the 36 settled same-day conflicts the displaced core entry outperformed the sleeve candidate over the sleeve's own matched horizon (median replacement value -0.87%). The positive mean (+1.45%) came from a right tail of supplier-financing and MOVE wins concentrated in old_thin. In late_strong -- the regime where cash is actually scarce and arbitration would bind -- displacement cost -8.07% mean per pair. Sleeves did beat the SPY control (+5.05% vs -0.14%), so sleeve candidates carry signal, but not more signal than the same-day core entry.
post_run_reflection.realized_failure_mode: core trend entries beat 10d sleeve holds on matched horizon
post_run_reflection.forbidden_near_neighbor_retry: Do not re-slice these 36 settled pairs by window, regime, sleeve, or sector to find a sub-population where arbitration 'works'; do not build a partial arbitration rule (score threshold, regime gate, sleeve whitelist) tuned on this settled cohort; do not swap in other sleeves or change horizons and rerun the same join.
post_run_reflection.new_evidence_required: Park entry-time cross-source slot arbitration. Reopen only with (a) at least 20 settled FORWARD same-day core-entry x sleeve-candidate conflict decisions recorded on the production allocator/daily default-off surface under unchanged policies (current forward conflict rate is near zero: the allocator snapshot ledger shows 0 candidates on most days), or (b) a genuinely different allocator mechanism that does not displace core entries, e.g. a pre-declared funding source that never depends on future core cash needs (per exp-20260716-009).
